_sources.snowshoe_hare: Lepus americanus, North American boreal forest and its montane fingers. Range roughly 36-70 N, 170-52 W [verify]. Densities cycle about every 10 years: lows near 0.1/ha, peaks of 1-6/ha (Krebs et al. 2001, Kluane, Yukon) [verify]. Lives under forest cover, so prairie, desert, tundra, rock, ice and water hold none.
_sources.white_tailed_deer: Odocoileus virginianus, southern Canada to northern South America, roughly 15 S-60 N, 168-34 W [verify]. Northern forest often 1-5/km2; farm-prairie edge 5-15/km2 [verify]. Scarce in open desert scrub. Tundra, rock, ice and water hold none.
_sources.moose: Alces alces (North American range only here; Eurasian elk to follow). Roughly 40-70 N, 168-52 W [verify]. Boreal forest often 0.1-2/km2, aspen-parkland edge of the prairie lower; none in desert, tundra above the shrubs, rock, ice or open water [verify].
_sources.canada_lynx: Lynx canadensis, roughly 42-70 N, 168-52 W [verify]. About 2-45 per 100 km2 depending on the hare cycle (Slough and Mowat 1996; Krebs et al.) [verify]. Follows the snowshoe hare 10-year cycle about 2 years behind (cycle_lag_years). Forest only.
_sources.note: Labelled calibration, not a census (PROJECT-RULES 5 and 7). Per hectare. A place picks a value inside its range from a hash of lat/lon and the cycle phase (hare) so the same place and year return the same row.
